title: Build a social listening digest
description: A system that pulls your brand's social mentions each week and turns them into a short digest of what people are saying and what needs a response.

pull.title: Pull
pull.content: Downloading the latest changes from GitHub to your computer so your local copy is up to date. Claude pulls before starting work to make sure it's building on the newest version, not an old one.

agent.title: Agent
agent.content: An AI that works independently to complete a goal — planning steps, picking tools, running them, and deciding what to do next without you prompting it at every step. Unlike a chatbot, an agent takes action.

model.title: Model
model.content: A specific trained version of an AI. Claude has several models (like Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) that differ in capability and speed. Larger models are smarter but slower; smaller ones are faster and cheaper.

skill.title: Skill
skill.content: A plain-text file with instructions for a specific repeatable workflow. Save it once, then trigger it with a slash command like /research-competitive. Same steps and output format every time — like a macro for Claude.

slack.title: Slack
slack.content: The team messaging app most companies run on. In Level 2, students connect Slack to their AI tools to trigger workflows from messages, post AI-generated updates to channels, or summarize threads automatically.

claude.title: Claude
claude.content: The AI made by Anthropic. Available as a chat tool at claude.ai, as a desktop app (Claude Desktop), and as a terminal tool (Claude Code). The different interfaces are suited for different types of work.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.content: The instruction or message you give to an AI. The quality of your prompt directly shapes the quality of the output. Writing better prompts is one of the highest-leverage skills in this program.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.content: The written definition of what a good output looks like, in 3–5 scoreable dimensions. Evals grade against a rubric; without one, 'is this good?' is a vibe, not a measurement.

chatgpt.title: ChatGPT
chatgpt.content: OpenAI's chat assistant. The most widely known AI tool — works similarly to Claude but with different strengths and weaknesses. Useful to have access to for cross-checking outputs or trying alternate models.

routine.title: Routine
routine.content: A cloud-based scheduled task that runs automatically even when your computer is off. Routines have access to tool connectors (Gmail, Slack, etc.) and can run on any schedule you set. In Level 3, routines are the heartbeat for Claude Code Dispatch agents — created via `/schedule` or `CronCreate`, they translate to standard cron syntax under the hood.

tool-connectors.title: Tool Connectors
tool-connectors.content: Integrations that let Claude read from and write to apps you use (Gmail, Slack, Google Calendar, Notion, HubSpot, etc.). Set up once in Customize → Connectors. Each connector opens up a new category of tasks Claude can automate.

children.text: AI adoption in marketing reached 86.4% in 2026, up from 41% two years earlier, per [HubSpot's State of Marketing Report](https://www.hubspot.com/state-of-marketing). Conversation about brands is rising alongside it, and scanning mentions by hand stops working past a handful of platforms. This system pulls your recent brand mentions and comments, groups them by theme and sentiment, and delivers a weekly digest naming what's new, what needs a response, and one quote worth reading in full.
Listening tools built for this already do the clustering. The build here is choosing what earns a place in the weekly summary. A digest someone opens beats a dashboard nobody checks.
Run it as a weekly paste-in [prompt](#tooltip-prompt), a saved skill, or a scheduled [agent](#tooltip-agent) that posts the digest to [Slack](#tooltip-slack).
Open your AI chat and have it interview you into a scope document. Done means a written scope naming where your mentions live, what counts as worth flagging, and who gets the digest.

children.prompt: I want to build a system with my AI tool that turns our brand mentions and comments each week into a short digest I can read. Ask me questions, one at a time, about where our mentions currently live, what counts as something worth flagging versus routine noise, how I want sentiment and themes grouped, and who should get the digest each week. When you have what you need, write it up as a scope document I can build from.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: the interview forces a definition of "worth flagging" before you're staring at fifty mentions, and that definition is the decision that shapes the output most.

items: Where your mentions currently live, a listening tool, manual platform searches, or somewhere else.
What counts as worth flagging versus [routine](#tooltip-routine) noise for your brand.
Who gets the digest and how fast a flagged item needs a response.

children.text: Bring the scope document. Pressure-test it first by pasting it into a fresh session or a different [model](#tooltip-model) and asking it to poke holes. Then gather any access it calls for. Common [connectors](#tooltip-tool-connectors) are a social listening tool if you have one (Sprout Social, Brandwatch, Meltwater), the platforms themselves if you don't (native search on X, Instagram, Reddit), and Slack or email for distribution. The paste-in version needs none.

**Create.** Start building the system your scope document describes, and test it on a real week of mentions. The prompt below is an example of the core task. Your scope document will give you a version shaped to your setup.

children.prompt:
Goal: Turn this week's brand mentions into a digest.

Context: Here are the mentions and comments collected this week: [paste export or summary from your listening tool]. We care most about [specific themes, e.g., product complaints, competitor comparisons, praise we could reuse].

Rules:
- Group by theme and sentiment, don't just list mentions chronologically.
- Flag anything that looks like it needs a direct response versus something that's just useful signal.
- Do not editorialize or add sentiment we didn't detect.
- Output format: a one-page digest with a themes-and-sentiment summary, a flagged-for-response list, and one notable quote worth reading in full.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: grouping by theme before sentiment keeps a recurring complaint visible instead of buried inside a scroll of one-off mentions.

children.text: **Review.** Check the output against your scope. Grouped by theme, response items flagged, quote worth using?
**Feedback.** Tell it exactly what it got wrong, a sarcastic comment read as praise, and fold the correction into the rules.

items: Track theme frequency over time to catch a slow-building issue before it spikes.
Add a reusable-quote flag for praise worth repurposing as social proof.

children.text: **Measure** with a [rubric](#tooltip-rubric). Have your AI chat turn the scope bar into pass/fail checks and a run log in one pass.

children.prompt: From my scope document, write a rubric for judging each weekly digest, with 4 to 6 pass/fail checks. Then set up a simple run log I can keep in a doc or spreadsheet, with columns for date, mentions reviewed, items flagged for response, flags that turned out to matter, and what rule I changed. Give me both in a format I can paste into my notes.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: pass/fail checks remove the judgment call, and the log columns make a recurring sentiment misread visible after a few weeks of entries.

children.text: **Log** every run against the rubric. Each entry takes a minute. Note the date, which rubric checks passed or failed, and what you changed. A single miss is noise, and a repeated miss is an instruction you haven't written yet.

**Make skills** from what the log shows. Once the system passes the rubric a few weeks straight, package the prompt and your corrected rules into a reusable AI skill, so every run starts from your defaults instead of a blank chat. When the log shows the same check failing again and again, that gap is a candidate for a skill of its own. [Claude](#tooltip-claude)'s built-in skill-creator skill will interview you and write the skill for you, and a custom GPT does the same in [ChatGPT](#tooltip-chatgpt).
One durable failure mode. It reads sarcasm and industry jargon as sentiment more often than you'd expect, so spot-check its calls every week rather than trusting the first read.
